findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the full set of tracker/<id> path-composition consumers outside _store/ (reducer/, _engine_support/, attest/, signing.py, metrics/, _snapshot/, llm/*, _io/, graph/, and the many _commands/* sites) and state that each is routed through the new layout helper.
evidence: Plan step 3 lists only 'replay, resolver, graph, lifecycle, compaction/fsck/sidecar readers, and reconciler-local ticket lookups'
search_files for os.path.join(tracker, ...) returns direct path composition across reducer/, _engine_support/, attest/, signing.py, metrics/, _snapshot/, llm/, _io/, and dozens of _commands/* files
search_files for 'tracker /' shows Path-idiom composition in llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:278, graph/_links.py:381, _snapshot/ticket_view.py, and many _commands/*
findings.finding: The step-3 consumer list omits many modules OUTSIDE _store/ that compose the ticket path directly (os.path.join(tracker, <id>) or tracker / <id>), all of which must be routed through the new layout helper: _ids.py (fast-path _existing_ticket_dir_name at :98/:183), reducer/_api.py & reducer/_inbound.py, _engine_support/ (lookups, reads, validate, next_batch, field_reads), attest/authorship.py, signing.py, metrics/blame.py, _snapshot/ticket_view.py, llm/overlap/queue.py, llm/enrich_drain.py, llm/completion_sidecar.py, llm/plan_review/{sidecar,relation_snapshot,claimability}.py, llm/code_review/sidecar.py, _io/{import,export}_ndjson.py, graph/{_links,_status,_cache,_hierarchy,_graph}.py, and numerous _commands/* (txn, transition, transition_close, claim, delete, compact, compact_recovery, fsck_scan, fsck_repair, identity, verify_authorship, session_log, close_precheck, close_disposition, compact_trigger).
scenarios: A ticket written under the sharded path is invisible to an un-updated reader (e.g. reducer, sidecar, graph walk), causing MISSING/unresolved reads
A migrated store breaks a command whose tracker/<id> join was not routed through the helper

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the resolver return contract (currently a separator-free single directory name, doubling as a path-injection barrier) is reconciled with a two-segment sharded path, and update/enumerate the os.path.join(tracker, resolved) call sites accordingly.
evidence: _ids.py:477 resolve_ticket_dir_name docstring: 'a single, separator-free segment contained in tracker_dir'
_ids.py:493-496: 'basename makes the separator-free guarantee explicit (and is a recognized path-injection barrier for the join the caller builds from the return value)'
Call sites join the bare name: e.g. tests and src use os.path.join(tracker, resolve_ticket_dir_name(ticket_id, tracker)); llm/overlap/queue.py:184 os.path.join(tracker, _resolve(ticket_id, tracker))
findings.finding: The plan does not address that the id resolver (resolve_ticket_id / resolve_ticket_dir_name in _ids.py) is contractually documented to return a SEPARATOR-FREE single directory NAME (backed by os.path.basename and cited as a CodeQL path-injection sanitizer), and that dozens of call sites do os.path.join(tracker, resolve_ticket_dir_name(...)). Sharding to tickets/<first-two-hex>/<id> makes the on-disk location a TWO-segment relative path, so either the resolver's return contract must change (breaking the separator-free/basename invariant and its path-injection barrier) or every join-site must derive the shard prefix itself.
scenarios: A caller joins the resolver's single-segment result to tracker and lands on a non-existent flat path after sharding
The security invariant (separator-free basename as injection barrier) is weakened if the resolver starts returning a path with a separator

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the sharded layout preserves short-id/prefix/full-id resolution (e.g. combined index spanning all shard subdirs, or a per-shard bisect), since today's resolver bisects a single flat sorted listing and does an O(1) sibling join.
evidence: _ids.py:294 `_dir_prefix_matches` bisects `sorted_names` (a flat listing) for a contiguous prefix run
_ids.py:236 `_scan_tracker_root` does one `os.listdir(tracker_dir)` and treats dir names as ids
_ids.py:85 `_existing_ticket_dir_name` joins `os.path.join(tracker_norm, name)` and isdir-checks — a one-level assumption
AC-2: 'Ticket resolution (alias, short-id, full-id) ... are unchanged'
findings.finding: The plan does not specify how short-id / generic-prefix resolution works under the sharded layout; today it relies on a single sorted flat listing of the tracker root plus a bisect over a contiguous prefix run (_ids.py `_dir_prefix_matches`, `_scan_tracker_root`, `build_resolver_scan_index`), and the fast O(1) `os.path.join(tracker, name)` exact-dir check — both of which assume all ticket dirs are direct siblings.
scenarios: Resolving an 8-hex short id or a >=4-char prefix against a sharded store
The close-precheck many-id walk that prebuilds ResolverScanIndex
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the layout helper to build the resolver's sorted-name index and exact-dir lookup across all fan-out shards, and update `_scan_tracker_root`/`_dir_prefix_matches`/`_existing_ticket_dir_name` to compose the shard segment, so short-id/prefix/full-id resolution and ambiguity handling are byte-identical to the flat case.

llm/enrich_drain.py:145/184/359 iterate `os.listdir(tracker)`

_commands/verify_authorship.py:417, _commands/identity.py:134/174, _commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:137, _io/export_ndjson.py:54, _store/store_usability.py:157, _commands/compact.py:259 all flat-scan the tracker root
Step 3 names only 'replay, resolver, graph, lifecycle, compaction/fsck/sidecar readers, and reconciler-local ticket lookups'

scenarios: Store maintenance walks (gitutil `_ticket_dirs`), enrich drain, authorship verification, identity listing, fsck health, ndjson export, store usability detection

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that, after a full ensure/migration run, no ticket remains at the legacy flat path (removal verified alongside the sharded replacement).
evidence: AC3 asserts 'all full ids/aliases survive and a second ensure run is a no-op'
Step 2 keeps reading flat paths 'until the migration has converged' but no AC verifies convergence (flat paths emptied) for a migrated store
findings.finding: AC3 verifies the sharded replacement and no-op re-run but does not assert removal/absence of the original flat paths after migration, leaving the migration's completeness (contract half) unproven.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 3 / Implementation Plan step 4
scenarios: Migration leaves stale flat copies alongside sharded ones; tree-churn reduction is undermined but tests still pass
findings.suggested_fix: Extend test_store_sharded_layout.py to assert the flat namespace is empty (or absent) post-migration for a fully-migrated store, complementing the survival/no-op checks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive step 3's consumer inventory from the symbol graph (find_referencing_symbols on resolve_ticket_dir_name plus a string grep for `tracker_dir`/flat-root `os.listdir` composition) and add the omitted metrics readers (event_metrics._ticket_dirs, sidecar_metrics, bug_trends._ticket_dirs) and llm/epic_bug_screen._first_claim_ts to the routed-through-helper list.
evidence: Plan step 3 enumerates consumers as: "replay, resolver, graph, lifecycle, compaction/fsck/sidecar readers, and reconciler-local ticket lookups" — a category list that names no metrics reader.

src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:48-62 `_ticket_dirs` does `for name in os.listdir(root): ... out.append(os.path.join(root, name))` treating each flat-root subdir as a ticket dir; consumed at lines 178/210/258/281.
src/rebar/metrics/sidecar_metrics.py:53 imports `_ticket_dirs` and iterates it (lines 116/166/230); src/rebar/metrics/bug_trends.py:57 defines its own `_ticket_dirs` walking the flat root (line 102).
src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py:127 `ticket_dir = _os.path.join(str(_config.tracker_dir(repo_root)), ticket_id)` composes a flat path directly.
findings.finding: The consumer inventory that must be re-routed off flat `tracker/<id>` composition (Implementation Plan step 3) omits the metrics module family and epic_bug_screen, both of which compose or iterate ticket directories against the flat root and are not covered by any named category (replay/resolver/graph/lifecycle/compaction/fsck/sidecar/reconciler).
findings.location: Implementation Plan, step 3: "Update replay, resolver, graph, lifecycle, compaction/fsck/sidecar readers, and reconciler-local ticket lookups to route through the shared helper instead of composing `tracker/<id>` directly."
scenarios: metrics/event_metrics._ticket_dirs: under sharding, os.listdir(root) yields shard dirs (tickets/ab), so event/session/status metrics iterate shard subtrees and os.path.basename returns a two-hex string as a bogus ticket id — silently wrong metrics, no error.
metrics/sidecar_metrics and metrics/bug_trends reuse the same flat-root iterator and break identically (review/completion counts, close timestamps).

llm/epic_bug_screen._first_claim_ts composes tracker/<id> directly; a migrated ticket now lives at tracker/<hex>/<id>, so os.path.isdir(ticket_dir) is False and the first-claim anchor is silently lost.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test fixture that triggers the ambiguous-collision case and asserts the migration refuses (does not lose or reassign any identity) rather than corrupting the store.
evidence: AC3: 'asserts all full ids/aliases survive and a second ensure run is a no-op' — happy path only.
Step 4 introduces behavior that 'refuses ambiguous collisions' with no corresponding test named.
findings.finding: Step 4 adds a new collision-refusal guard, but no acceptance criterion or named test exercises that error path — the ACs only cover the happy migration (all ids survive, no-op re-run). The new failure branch of the migration goes untested.
scenarios: A fixture with two ids that shard to a colliding path: without a test, the refuse-vs-corrupt behavior of the migration is unverified and could silently drop or overwrite a ticket identity.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the back-out story for a MIGRATED store: name that the sharded layout is not backward-readable by pre-shard code (a code-version floor), and add a heldout assertion on the post-rollback/downgrade read state (or an explicit `DATA LOSS RISK` note) so the deferred live cutover inherits the rollback facts.
evidence: Step 4: 'migrates existing flat ticket directories into the sharded namespace ... tree-checks before committing, preserves all directory names/event bytes'

Step 2 only provides forward compatibility: 'publish new events under the sharded path while still reading existing flat paths' — new code reads both, but the reverse (old code reading a migrated store) is not addressed

Code fact: staging.stage_event composes os.path.join(tracker, ticket_id) directly (src/rebar/_store/staging.py:238), so pre-shard readers resolve only flat paths and would silently miss migrated tickets
AC3 asserts identity survives and re-run is a no-op, but never asserts the state a reader observes AFTER a rollback / code downgrade of a migrated store
findings.finding: The in-place layout migration rewrites record locations (flat tracker/<id> -> sharded), but the plan specifies only the forward-read compatibility (new code reads both layouts) and asserts no post-rollback/downgrade state: un-upgraded readers that compose tracker/<id> directly cannot resolve migrated tickets, and no back-out path or code-version floor is named for a migrated store.
findings.location: Implementation Plan step 4 + Acceptance Criteria line 3 ('a migration maps existing flat paths ... without losing or reassigning any ticket identity')
scenarios: Operator (per the out-of-scope live cutover) migrates the live .tickets-tracker, then rolls back to pre-shard code and tickets appear to vanish
A mixed fleet where some readers run old code against a migrated store

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define what an 'ambiguous collision' is under the shard scheme and add a fixture asserting the migration refuses (errors, does not reassign identity) on that case.
evidence: 'refuses ambiguous collisions' is stated as a behavior
No definition of when two flat ids collide in the sharded namespace, and no AC verifies the refusal/error behavior
findings.finding: Step 4 requires the migration to 'refuse ambiguous collisions' but the plan never defines what constitutes an ambiguous collision under the fan-out scheme, and no acceptance criterion exercises the refusal path.
scenarios: A migration encounters a collision case the executor did not anticipate; behavior is unspecified and untested
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that since the shard prefix derives deterministically from the id, a collision means two distinct source paths mapping to the same target; add a RED fixture proving the ensure-registry aborts without mutating on such a case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete pass threshold for AC1 (e.g. root-tree bytes for a single-ticket mutation drop by >= N% or below B bytes on the fixture) so the test assertion is deterministic.
evidence: 'proves the root-tree bytes drop substantially versus an equivalent flat layout'
No numeric target or percentage stated for the reduction the fixture must demonstrate
findings.finding: AC1's pass condition uses the subjective term 'substantially' with no numeric threshold, so the test author must invent an unstated bar.
scenarios: A tiny reduction technically passes 'substantially'; a reviewer cannot tell if the outcome was met
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'drop substantially' with a concrete assertion, e.g. 'the re-emitted top-level tree for a single-ticket mutation is < X bytes and at least 80% smaller than the flat root tree'.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the ensure-registry migration runs under the existing store write lock (or otherwise serialize it against writers) so the read-then-commit cannot race a concurrent flat-path publish.
evidence: Step 4: 'tree-checks before committing ... and is safe to re-run'
AC-3: 'a second ensure run is a no-op'
stage_event (_store/staging.py:238) publishes under `os.path.join(tracker, ticket_id)` with no lock held at stage time; the write lock is held at promote
findings.finding: The migration's 'tree-check before committing' plus 'second ensure run is a no-op' is a check-then-act sequence whose ordering relative to the store write lock is unstated, leaving a potential window where a concurrent flat-path writer strands a ticket in the old layout.
scenarios: A writer publishing a new event under the (still-supported) flat path while the ensure-registry migration reads the flat set and commits the sharded set

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure-disposition of the ambiguous-collision refusal: does it abort the migration atomically (fatal/permanent, no partial writes) or skip-and-continue, and what the caller observes.
evidence: 'refuses ambiguous collisions, and is safe to re-run'
No disposition word (fatal/permanent vs retryable) is attached to the collision-refusal arm.
findings.finding: The migration introduces an ambiguous-collision refusal path (step 4: 'refuses ambiguous collisions') but the plan never states its caller-facing disposition — whether a collision aborts the whole migration as a fatal/permanent error the operator must resolve, or is skippable/retryable.
scenarios: Two flat ticket ids shard to the same target and collide: the plan does not say whether the migration aborts entirely (fatal), leaving the store partially migrated, or skips the pair and continues.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line disposition contract: 'an ambiguous collision aborts the ensure run atomically as a fatal error (no partial tree written); the operator resolves the collision before re-running.'

No documentation deliverable is listed for the layout decision
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new on-disk tree-layout contract spanning replay, resolver, graph, lifecycle, compaction/fsck/sidecar readers with no ADR/design-doc/AGENTS.md capture of the sharding decision.
